title: Pan con Tomate
subtitle: Grilled bread rubbed with garlic and ripe tomato, finished with good olive oil
excerpt: Toasted bread rubbed hard with a cut clove of garlic and then with a ripe tomato, drizzled with olive oil and a little black pepper.
sourceNotes: A staple of Catalan cooking, eaten at breakfast and as a base for tapas across Spain.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 and takes 10 minutes. There is very little cooking involved: the work is in the quality of the ingredients. Use the ripest, most flavourful tomatoes you can find, bread that has some crust and chew, and the best olive oil you own.

The tomato is rubbed directly onto the surface of the toasted bread until the flesh is completely worked in and only the skin remains. Press firmly and use a circular motion. The bread should be stained red and feel slightly damp, not wet. Do not slice or chop the tomato: halving it and rubbing is the only correct method.

items.prepNote: very ripe, halved across the equator

content.text: Heat a griddle pan over a high heat until very hot. Cut thick slices of crusty bread. Place them on the griddle and press down gently. Toast for 2 minutes per side until char marks form and the surface is properly crisp. Work in batches if needed.

While the bread is still hot, rub the cut side of a halved garlic clove firmly across the entire surface of each slice. The rough toast will grate the garlic into it. Use as much or as little as you like.

Take a halved tomato and rub the cut face firmly over the garlicky surface using a circular motion. Press hard so the flesh breaks down into the bread. Keep rubbing until almost all the flesh is worked in. Discard the skin.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and season with black pepper. Serve immediately while the bread is still warm. Do not let it sit or the base will become soggy.

items.solution: It was assembled too far ahead or the tomatoes were too watery. Use dry, meaty tomatoes and assemble just before serving.

items.problem: The garlic flavour is too harsh
items.solution: Use a lighter touch when rubbing the garlic. One pass across the surface is enough for a background note. For very mild garlic flavour, rub with the cut side of garlic without pressing down.

items.problem: The tomato is not rubbing into the bread properly
items.solution: The tomatoes are not ripe enough. A firm, underripe tomato will not break down. Leave them at room temperature for a day or two until fully soft and fragrant.

content.text: is from Catalonia and is one of the most uncomplicated things in Spanish cooking. It appears at breakfast alongside coffee, as a base for anchovies or cured meat, and as a starter before a larger meal. The quality of the tomatoes is everything. In summer, when tomatoes are at their peak, it is one of the best things you can eat. Outside of tomato season, it is worth making only with the ripest ones you can track down.
